Case Study - Research & Product Design

Next Gen Contact Center Web App

A unified, AI-orchestrated desktop that transforms the customer and employee journey. Centralizing all customer interactions to maximize rep effectiveness and deliver proactive, best-in-class customer experiences.

Sector

Telecom · Conversational AI · Enterprise Customer Care

My Role

Led research and UX strategy for a 35K-rep unification effort; owned the Service Change redesign end-to-end, from research to shipped product

Scale

35K+ reps · 100M+ customers

01 - The Problem

One disconnect, three places it shows up

Customer experience

Transfers, long contacts and inconsistent answers depending on who picks up.

Rep performance

Reps juggle multiple systems while actively hunting for information mid-call.

Business value

Multiple applications to maintain, heavy on development, light on workforce flexibility.

35K+
Reps across voice, chat and social
100M+
Customers across mobile and home internet
2

04 - Research Approach

An ongoing research practice, not a one-off study

01

Call listening

5 to 15 recorded support calls reviewed every month, voice-first, across both platforms.

02

Call volume data analytics

Quantitative analysis of call volume and intent data across the contact center, surfacing troubleshooting as the single largest driver.

03

1:1 rep interviews

Recurring voice-of-rep interview program feeding directly into design decisions.

04

Interactive step-mapping

Compared the two legacy platforms' troubleshooting flows step by step to find shared logic.

05

Quarterly field visits

In-person observation of reps on the floor, done in batches every quarter.

Nine capabilities, organized around what mattered most

The unified desktop's scope, seen through the same three lenses used to frame the problem: what it does for the customer, for the rep and for the business.

Customer experience

Common customer account views

A consistent view of shared customers and their services, with permissions-based access.

Competitive comparisons

Integrated comparisons and guided calculators supporting product, service and value conversations.

One order, all products

Any product or service fulfilled through a single order for any customer.

Rep performance

Core AI enablement

Shared, customer-centric AI capabilities across product lines, with built-in feedback loops.

Dynamic, active UI/UX

Personalized journeys with an interface that adapts to guide reps through each interaction.

Message and social integration

Messaging and social channels consolidated into the rep's primary tool.

Business value

Convergence and integration

A foundation built for future expansion and a framework for third-party integrations.

Permissions

A role-based engine with flexibility over employee access to accounts, products and services.

Non-technical maintenance

Configuration tools that let operations update content and capabilities without engineering work.

06 - Concept Exploration

Three directions, three different bets on AI vs. rep control

Canvas playground

  • A single infinite canvas
  • AI-generated contextual cards
  • Highly customizable, less guided

The agentic way

  • AI proactively works the problem
  • Transparent, step-by-step AI reasoning
  • Powerful, but asks reps to trust AI more

Bi-modal framework

  • Guided flow plus a flexible workspace
  • Progressive disclosure of detail
  • AI as a team player, not the driver

Bi-modal won because it was the only direction that let reps keep control while still getting AI's speed.

07 - Grounding the Design

One real scenario made the problem impossible to hand-wave

Concepts stayed tied to real, high-frequency calls, not hypotheticals. This one shows the "two systems, one job" problem at its sharpest:

A customer needs to close one line, settle a final balance and move a second account onto autopay - a request that spans two separate systems today.

Hero scenario - "Disconnect & Autopay"

The storyboard we built from scenarios like this: a customer's issue triggers the flow, an AI assistant greets and starts understanding it, then a seamless handover to a rep with full context already loaded (no re-explaining) and the rep resolves with everything already in view.

08 - Trade-offs, Challenges & Constraints

Two moments where the honest answer was friction, not consensus

01

Pushing back on engineering leadership's AI-first instinct

Their read was "lead with new AI capability." I brought the call-volume data and the 90%-identical-logic finding to argue for unifying the foundation first. Trade-off: a less flashy pitch internally, in exchange for a direction the data actually supported.

02

Advocating for reps against an engineering-driven POC

When platform engineering built their first POC, we moved fast to assess it against real user needs, brought it into a field visit so reps could react to it directly and fed concrete recommendations and design back to engineering. Trade-off: challenging a build already in motion, on a compressed timeline, with only partial documentation to point back to.

The friction was real, but so was the outcome - in April 2026 the work behind this project was formally recognized by Verizon leadership.

09 - Field Validation

Testing the concept with the reps who'd actually use it, voice first

What we tested for

  • Comprehension - do reps understand the new UI and terms?
  • Sufficiency - is on-screen info enough to act, without switching tools?
  • Utility - which parts actually help reps do their job?
  • AI behavior - does AI content beside a live call confuse or mislead?

Methodology

  • 9 reps tested - 4 on voice as the primary read, 5 on chat as a secondary check
  • 20 to 30 minute 1-on-1 sessions
  • Rapid flash testing across scenarios rather than one long interview, to cover more ground
Previously we needed to open the digital and check for all the things... now it has been added. So it is easy to check and we can easily convey to the customer.

Rep feedback - one screen beats six tabs

11 - Reflection

What this project reinforced for me

01

Data beats instinct

The loudest opinion in the room isn't always the right priority - call-volume data settled a real disagreement about where to start.

02

AI needs a human check

AI-assisted synthesis is genuinely fast, but every output still needed validation against real interviews and field visits before I trusted it.

03

Simplifying is its own kind of design

Untangling two years of legacy complexity into one clear flow was as hard and as valuable as inventing something new.

Behind Research Approach

Call volume data analytics

Leadership was fascinated by general AI capabilities, but the data definitively showed that "Troubleshooting" was the massive volume driver, at 1,044,018 calls. We had to fix the foundation first.

Top L3 intents

From data to synthesis

Using this data and call transcripts, with AI assistance, I synthesized personas and journey maps for both the customer and the rep. The transcripts only captured what was said out loud, though - they missed the part where the rep was navigating across multiple systems to actually resolve the query.

Behind Research Approach

1:1 rep interviews

A recurring interview program, structured around the same core topics every time so patterns could build across reps and over time.

Topics touched

  • Typical workday
  • Call volume and metrics
  • Team structure and collaboration
  • Troubleshooting process
  • Common issues
  • Key information and tools for troubleshooting
  • Biggest challenges
  • Effective features of ACSS
  • New functionalities
  • Acronyms and jargon
  • Handling difficult customers
  • Overall system evolution

Sample questions

  • Can you tell me about yourself and the roles and responsibilities that you currently perform?
  • Can you describe your typical day at work? (Key activities)
  • What did you do when you first came into the office today and started working?
  • How many calls do you handle? What is the target?
  • What are the key tasks you perform within ACSS?
  • According to you, what works well in the current application and what doesn't?
  • How do you go about solving things which do not work for you?
  • Do you employ any shortcuts while performing the tasks? If yes, what are those?
  • How do you first understand the customer's issue and narrow down the focus area to find the underlying cause(s)?
  • How do you troubleshoot a specific issue? What are the problems you face?

Behind Research Approach

Interactive step-mapping

I led Knowledge Transfer (KT) sessions comparing ACSS (Wireless) and Optix (Wireline) step-by-step troubleshooting flows for a "Home Internet Not Working" scenario. We mapped out every step and uncovered our biggest breakthrough: the underlying logic was 90% identical across Wireless and Wireline.

Behind Research Approach

Quarterly field visits

In the field visits, alongside testing new experiences and concepts, we also worked to enrich existing artifacts - this is where we validated and enriched the rep journey map, persona and a day in the life of a rep.

Rep journey map

  • 1
    Clarify and expand customer labels

    Change tags like "senior" to explicitly state "senior citizen" or "age" - reps currently misread it as customer tenure (e.g. 5 years) and couldn't parse "Churn elevated" either.

  • 2
    Detail info

    Reps expect more detail when a line expands - it would make upgrading and managing easier.

  • 3
    Adjust billing detail visibility

    Reps handle billing concerns constantly and need quick access to specific line-level charges - international fees, activation fees, autopay status, payment due.

  • 4
    Network status

    Show service outage status with the address and sync it directly with the network.

  • 5
    Missing customer insights

    Reps already rely on the existing customer insights section in ACSS and expect offers or upselling opportunities here too.

  • 6
    Login time

    Reps want login and break timings surfaced upfront.

The same testing round also covered this AI-suggested "Update address" insight card, surfaced mid-call when a customer asks to update their address.
